newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent steadies at higher levels after APIs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent steadies at higher levels after APIs.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures steadied at higher levels after the overnight release of mildly bullshi data from the American Petroleum Institute (API,) traders said.
June Brent stood 15 cents up at 1139 GMT, 15 cents up on the day, after a sharp fall on Tuesday. Gas oil was unchanged at $163.75 a tonne.
"The APIs brought us up and it is probably also a little bit of a correction to yesterday's sharp fall," one IPE dealer said.
The API data showed a weekly fall in U.S. middle distillate inventories of nearly 4.7 million barrels.
That compared to earlier expectations of a half-million barrel drawdown.
Gasoline stocks were 1.9 million barrels down week-on-week, and the API report also revised downwards the previous week's inventory levels by 3.1 million barrels.
GNI research urged some caution in interpreting the API data as "the demand figures have been jumping around recently" but added: "the data is positive nevertheless."
"Similarly the recent cool weather has lifted distillate demand to a whacking 4.2 million barrels per day against last week's 3.27 million," the company said in a daily report.

"With supplies in some areas moderately tight and considering the minor drop in refinery runs, the products should derive some support from this data. There should also be some spillover into crude prices."
Traders said they saw resistance firstly up at around $18.22 then $18.30, followed by much stronger resistance at a chart gap between $18.64 and $18.77.
